feature: ai-git-cleanup v2: one gate, fetch status, post-cleanup sync
summary: Merge the ai-git-cleanup skill's two confirmation gates into a single plan-and-approve view, surface whether the initial git fetch succeeded, and fold the post-cleanup local sync commands (worktree prune, ff-only pull, ahead report) into the same one approved plan — local git only, never zero confirmations.
plain_summary: When a feature is finished, the cleanup shows one complete plan of what it will remove and what it will sync, asks you once, and only then acts.
gating: Work checkpoints in order. Within a checkpoint, the gates run in order: behavior, then ui, then review. A checkpoint is "passed" only when every gate is "passed" or "n/a". Do not start checkpoint N+1 until checkpoint N has passed.

checkpoints.title: Merge the two confirmation gates and surface fetch status
checkpoints.goal: SKILL.md asks exactly once: one view presents the full analysis table with the per-row command plan (worktree removals first, then guard-paired deletes) and a single ask (delete all recommended / pick / stop); analyze.mjs emits a top-level fetchStatus that the gate displays; every execution guard is unchanged and the unit and structure specs are green.

plain.what: One view shows every recommended removal with its command, then asks for approval once.
plain.why: Two prompts meant approval could happen without the full plan on screen.
plain.check: Run the skill on a finished feature: you answer one question before anything changes.

tasks: skills/ai-git-cleanup/scripts/analyze.mjs: capture the exit of the best-effort `git fetch --prune origin` and add a top-level `fetchStatus` field — `ok` when the fetch succeeded or no origin exists, `failed: <first stderr line, trimmed>` when it failed — keeping stdout one single JSON document.

skills/ai-git-cleanup/SKILL.md: replace the gate 1 and gate 2 steps with ONE gate: a single view presenting the full analysis table with the exact per-row command plan (worktree removals first, then each `git merge-base --is-ancestor` guard paired with its `git branch -d`), followed by one `ask` (delete all recommended / pick / stop). State the hard floor: one explicit approval is always required, never zero, no auto-deletion.

skills/ai-git-cleanup/SKILL.md: display fetchStatus in that gate view, with a visible callout that a failed fetch means remote-derived states may be stale (classification already errs toward KEEP/needsReview — make it visible, not silent). Update the frontmatter description and 'What it produces' from two gates to one; keep disable-model-invocation, LicenseRef-Attributed and the Lifecycle block untouched.

Keep every execution rule verbatim in the rewritten steps: the guard runs immediately before every `-d`; `-D` only for evidence-backed claims that survived refutation; dirty worktree refused without explicit data-loss acknowledgment; protected/current/default never deletable; deletions only in the main session; no push, no reflog GC, no git gc, no CI.

tests/git-cleanup-analyze.spec.ts: assert fetchStatus in its exact configurations (R3) — `ok` with a working origin, `ok` with no origin, `failed: <reason>` with a broken origin — plus every field the gate consumes (R2).
tests/git-cleanup-cli.spec.ts: extend the no-origin and broken-origin tests with the exact fetchStatus values; fix comments that still say 'gate 2'.
Run bun scripts/gen-assets.ts after the SKILL.md/script edits, then the verify list.
acceptance: analyze.mjs output always carries fetchStatus: `ok` for a successful fetch or an absent origin, `failed: <reason>` when fetch fails, stdout still a single JSON document.
SKILL.md contains exactly one `ask` before execution; the view pairs the analysis table with the per-row command plan, worktree removals before guard-paired branch deletes.
The gate view shows fetchStatus and calls out that a failed fetch means remote-derived states may be stale.
The hard floor is stated: one explicit approval is always required; no auto-deletion, ever.
Execution invariants unchanged: guard immediately before every `-d`, `-D` only with named evidence, dirty worktree refused without data-loss acknowledgment, protected/current/default never deletable.

bun test tests/git-cleanup-analyze.spec.ts, tests/git-cleanup-cli.spec.ts, tests/skills.spec.ts and tests/embed-canon.spec.ts pass; bun run typecheck and bun run lint are clean (only the 3 pre-existing warnings in doctor-command.spec.ts).

checkpoints.title: Add post-cleanup sync to the approved plan and close docs
checkpoints.goal: The single approved plan carries the post-cleanup local sync — `git worktree prune` only if a worktree was removed, `git pull --ff-only` on the default branch only if it is behind its upstream, ahead reported never pushed — the flow spec proves the pairing contract and every invariant end to end, and the feature closes with CHANGELOG, an amended changeset and a green full sweep.

plain.what: The approved plan also brings your main files up to date after cleanup.
plain.why: Without it, you finish cleanup and must run the sync commands yourself.
plain.check: After a cleanup, your main branch is current without typing anything more.

tasks: skills/ai-git-cleanup/scripts/analyze.mjs: add a `postSync` section to the JSON — the exact `git worktree prune` command present only when a worktree removal is queued, the exact `git pull --ff-only` command present only when the default branch is behind its upstream (with the upstream name and behind count), and the ahead count for report-only output.

skills/ai-git-cleanup/SKILL.md: extend the single gate's plan with the post-cleanup lines in execution order — approved deletions (worktree removals, then guard-paired deletes), then `git worktree prune` if a worktree was removed, then `git pull --ff-only` on the default branch if it is behind, then an ahead report. The one ask covers these commands; ahead → report only, NEVER push. Invariants stay: no `git push`/`push --delete`, no reflog GC, no `git gc`, no CI, no auto-deletion.

tests/git-cleanup-flow.spec.ts: keep the pairing contract provable under the merged single-plan format (U16): every queued worktree removal precedes its branch delete with the candidate↔worktree back-link intact. Assert the new fields (R2): postSync.prune only when a worktree removal exists, postSync.pull only when the default is behind, ahead reported with no push command, fetchStatus present.

tests/git-cleanup-flow.spec.ts and tests/git-cleanup-analyze.spec.ts: guard each invariant in its exact configuration (R3) — assert the emitted document and SKILL.md never contain `git push`, `push --delete`, `git gc` or reflog GC, and that the dirty worktree refusal outranks the ordering.

CHANGELOG.md: amend the Unreleased ai-git-cleanup line to the single-approval flow and add the fetch-status and post-cleanup sync behaviour; amend the still-present unreleased .changeset/ai-git-cleanup.md (minor) instead of adding a second changeset; confirm package.json gains no dependency.
Run bun scripts/gen-assets.ts after the SKILL.md/script edits, then the full verify sweep in order: the three git-cleanup specs, skills, workflow-handoff, arch, embed-canon, then typecheck and lint.
acceptance: The one approved plan contains the sync commands in execution order: deletions, then prune (only if a worktree was removed), then ff-only pull (only if the default branch is behind), then the ahead report.
postSync fields are emitted only in their qualifying configurations; an ahead default branch is reported and never pushed.
The flow spec still proves the pairing contract: worktree removals ordered before their branch deletes, refusal outranking ordering for dirty worktrees.
No `git push`, `push --delete`, reflog GC, `git gc`, CI or auto-deletion exists anywhere in the skill or its emitted output.
CHANGELOG.md names the single-gate flow under Unreleased; .changeset/ai-git-cleanup.md is amended with a minor bump; package.json is unchanged.

bun test tests/git-cleanup-flow.spec.ts, tests/git-cleanup-analyze.spec.ts, tests/git-cleanup-cli.spec.ts, tests/skills.spec.ts, tests/workflow-handoff.spec.ts, tests/arch.spec.ts, tests/embed-canon.spec.ts, bun run typecheck and bun run lint all pass.

assumptions: The prior changeset .changeset/ai-git-cleanup.md still exists and CHANGELOG's Unreleased section still carries the original line, so it is amended rather than replaced by a new file (checked on disk; feature request says verify first).
One gate keeps the hard floor: exactly one explicit ask before any change, with delete-all / pick / stop, and stop before the ask leaves everything untouched (feature request).

fetchStatus is `ok` when no origin exists: with no remote there is no remote-derived state that could be stale, and the feature named only the two values ok and failed (feature request; analyze.mjs best-effort fetch).
A failed fetch's reason is the first trimmed stderr line of git fetch, so the gate shows something actionable instead of a bare flag (feature request asks for `failed: <reason>`).

The post-cleanup commands are emitted by analyze.mjs as postSync fields rather than hardcoded prose in SKILL.md, so every executed field is machine-assertable; conditionals are encoded by field presence (LEARNINGS R2/R3).
The default branch's ahead state is report-only in the analyzer and SKILL.md: pushing is out of scope forever, not a follow-up (feature request invariant).

The flow spec's U16 pairing contract is re-asserted as data (removal precedes delete, candidate↔worktree back-link) even though presentation merges into one view; only the textual 'gate 2' wording moves (tests/git-cleanup-flow.spec.ts U16 note).
No test pins the phrase 'two gates': a grep of tests/ finds only comments referencing gate 2, so rewording SKILL.md breaks no assertion, but comments are updated for truthfulness (tests/ grep).
Every checkpoint has ui null and gates.ui n/a — no UI anywhere; frontmatter keeps disable-model-invocation (feature request).

Verify uses targeted specs plus typecheck and lint per checkpoint, with the full structure sweep (skills, workflow-handoff, arch, embed-canon) in checkpoint 2's gate, matching the prior run's pattern; baseline at merge is 895/895 green with 3 pre-existing warnings in doctor-command.spec.ts (feature baseline).
No new dependencies are needed; confirm against package.json when closing checkpoint 2 (feature request; ladder: nothing here needs a package).
Sizes go s → m: checkpoint 1 is edits to two existing files plus two specs, checkpoint 2 adds the sync feature, flow spec and docs sweep (agents/checkpoint-planner.md sizes never shrink).
FILEMAP.md, AGENTS.md, LEARNINGS.md and README.md stay unchanged: they index skills as a whole, as in the prior run (prior plan assumption, still true).
notes: Out of scope, unchanged: remote branch deletion, push of any kind, reflog GC, git gc, CI integration, auto-deletion.
No fetch retry or deeper staleness model: one best-effort fetch, failure surfaced visibly, classification already errs conservative (feature request: visible, not silent).
The interactive pick option inside the single ask is unchanged from gate 1's original options; only the second confirmation disappears.

Test-count bookkeeping stays in .ai-engineering/workflow/test-plans/, written by the orchestrator's test-plan step — the checkpoint schema has no count field (agents/checkpoint-planner.md; viewer.html).
